title: DB Access Receipts
user: Teams letting tools or agents query production-adjacent databases who need per-query approval boundaries and a readable audit receipt without replacing their database client.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN asks whether giving AI agents database access is becoming the new BI-tool problem.
A separate Ask HN asks why it remains difficult for LLMs to query NoSQL databases.

recurrence: Two separate 2026 requests put database access and agent/tool usability in tension; the severity includes accidental data exposure and writes.
current_workaround: Create broad read-only credentials, copy results into chat, or forbid access entirely.
incumbents_and_gap: Retool, Metabase, and database proxies manage access broadly; teams still lack a lightweight local approval-and-receipt layer suited to tool-mediated exploratory queries.
smallest_useful_product: A local proxy/CLI with named allowlisted query templates, row/column caps, mandatory human confirmation for novel queries, and signed JSON audit receipts.
success_measure: Every pilot query has an attributable receipt, and zero unapproved write queries pass through the proxy during a 30-day trial.
monetization: one-time — security-conscious teams favor a local auditable tool over recurring data access fees.
constraints: No LLM required; parameterize queries; secret storage via OS keychain; receipts must avoid storing result data by default.
why_distinct: It constrains and proves database access instead of adding an AI query interface.
